basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 7.' and it opens '(Vers. 7.) Filii Regma, Saba et Dadan. Hic Saba per SIN (ש) litteram scribitur, supra'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 7.) Filii Regma, Saba et Dadan. Hic Saba per SIN (ש) litteram scribitur, supra vero per SAMECH (ס), a quo diximus appellatos Sabaeos. Interpretatur vero nunc Saba, Arabia, nam in septuagesimo primo psalmo, ubi nos habemus, Reges Arabum et Saba munera offerent: in Hebraeo scriptum est, Reges Saba, et Saba: primum nomen per SIN, secundum per SAMECH. Dadan gens est Aethiopiae in occidentali plaga.
